elements.quote: Interventions integrating non-communicable disease prevention and reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health: A systematic review
elements.reason: The title and text explicitly identify the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: In this systematic review, we evaluated the effectiveness of integrating gestational and non-gestational noncommunicable diseases interventions and RMNCH care among women and children in low- and middle-income countries.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit statement of the main objective.

elements.quote: This systematic review included randomized and quasirandomized controlled trials published from 2000 to 2015. Participants included reproductiveage women, children < 5 years old, and RMNCH care providers.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies inclusion criteria but does not explicitly state exclusion criteria.
The abstract does not identify the information sources used or the date they were last searched.
The abstract does not specify the methods used to assess risk of bias.
The abstract does not specify the methods used to present and synthesize the results.

elements.quote: We analyzed six studies from 7,949 retrieved articles.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies but does not report the number of participants.

elements.quote: Yoga exercise ( p < 0.01) and nutritional improvements ( p < 0.05) were effective in reducing gestational hypertension and diabetes.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes.
The discussion states a meta-analysis was not conducted due to differing interventions and small sample sizes.

elements.quote: Yoga exercise ( p < 0.01) and nutritional improvements ( p < 0.05) were effective in reducing gestational hypertension and diabetes.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect (reducing) and favors the intervention groups.

elements.quote: However, as primary evidence is scarce, further research on the effectiveness of integrating non-communicable disease prevention and RMNCH care is warranted.
elements.reason: The abstract briefly summarizes limitations regarding the scarcity of primary evidence.

elements.quote: Interventions that integrate non-communicable disease care/screening and RMNCH care may positively impact the health of women and children in low- and middle-income countries.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.

elements.quote: However, no prior systematic review article or protocol is available in this area, and the current integration status in these countries is unclear.

elements.quote: However, no prior systematic review article or protocol is available in this area, and the current integration status in these countries is unclear. elements.quote: Both assessed studies lacked information related to the blinding during data collection or implementation. All other biases were "low" in the selected studies. However, high attrition bias was observed in the Jayashree-Rakhshani study, because the dropout rate was almost 35% of the randomized participants in the intervention group ( 27,32 ). Table 2 shows the risk of bias in the four nonrandomized intervention studies. The overall risks of bias were "moderate" in the studies by Moon et al. and Aalami et al. ( 26,30 ), and "serious" for the studies by Plotkin et al. and Luo et al ( 29,31 ).
elements.reason: The text explicitly details the risk of bias (limitations) of the included studies, identifying specific issues such as lack of blinding, high attrition, and serious bias in non-randomized studies.
